blocks.text: The bar: a blender prop reads as made from the player's feet: a crate with bitten edges and a crack web across one plank, a statue missing a chunk of shoulder with centuries eaten off its rim, a bridge whose cables sag, a shrine roof sitting on its walls with no daylight at the gable. Every junction seated, every material slot named for the surface the game mounts on it, every claim checked in a rendered still you looked at, never an exit code. Budget triangles against three anchors: most things a game shows are under 20k each, a finished game plays about half a million in frame, a heavy scene one to two million; a hero piece the player stands beside earns more, its edges read from a metre. Plan the whole asset first (parts and sizes, slots by name); one script (→workshop) builds it, renders one full-size proof, exports the .glb; look once, fix that script, rerun, upload, place, return. A prop is done once placed, not when its still is perfect; a building a body walks into earns a second look-fix round once placed. A CHARACTER is the same build with a body in it, one skin that reads as its art style's character, never a pile of parts: a face and hands with anatomy, armour seated on the shoulders it was fitted to, cloth hanging between the legs, a weapon in the hand gripping it, moving on its own rig, in the api's order line.

import bpy, qm scene = bpy.context.scene scene.render.engine, scene.cycles.samples = "CYCLES", 8 # render.opengl refuses under -b; EEVEE renders in software scene.render.resolution_x = scene.render.resolution_y = 656 wall = bpy.data.objects["Wall"] # JOINED blocks = islands; damage a duplicate, keep the pristine original dmg = wall.data.attributes.new("dmg", "BOOLEAN", "POINT") dmg.data.foreach_set("value", [v.co.x > 0 for v in wall.data.vertices]) qm.qm_apply(wall, "chunks", selection_attr="dmg") # bites only the selected blocks; new faces take the LAST material slot qm.qm_apply(wall, "cracks", Scale=4.0) # params by socket name for name, cam in (("a", "Cam34"), ("b", "CamGable"), ("c", "CamTop")): # a turnaround: three 656-px views fill see's 2000 px, one alone renders at 1568 scene.camera = bpy.data.objects[cam] scene.render.filepath = f"/tmp/proof/wall_{name}.png" bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True) bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath="/workspace/wall.glb", export_apply=True) dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get(); print("tris", sum(len(o.evaluated_get(dg).data.loop_triangles) for o in scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"))

Then montage /tmp/proof/wall_*.png -tile 3x1 -geometry +4+4 /tmp/proof/wall.png && spawn see /tmp/proof/wall.png. Once the .glb is placed, mount a texture on every named slot (model.materials.<slot>.texture: "cdn/texture-<what>.png"); placeholder grey outside a flat style is unfinished.

import bpy, json # art/knight/build.py: the character's one pass C = json.load(open("art/knight/contract.json")) # {"unit": "m", "height": 1.9, "feet": 0, "up": "+Z", "front": "-Y", "forward": "+z", "tris": 12000} bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath="/workspace/knight/body.glb") # the body: mpfb (→api), your own, or a CDN base (→geometry) body = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH" and o.vertex_groups) # the skinned body, never the importer's bone widgets dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get(); zs = sorted((body.matrix_world @ v.co).z for v in body.evaluated_get(dg).data.vertices) # the deformed body in world space renders; body.scale moves a node no viewer draws s = C["height"] / (zs[-1] - zs[0]); (body.find_armature() or body).scale = (s, s, s); bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="SELECT"); bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True) # metres at scale 1; A = landmarks (hip, chest, shoulder) → anatomy.json rig = mixamo_armature(A) for o in (body, cuirass(A), pauldron(A, "L"), pauldron(A, "R"), gambeson(A)): o.modifiers.new("skin", "ARMATURE").object = rig sword = longsword(); sword.parent, sword.parent_type, sword.parent_bone = rig, "BONE", "RightHand" # the shield on LeftForeArm for name, keys in CLIPS.items(): # each clip, idle too, solved with none live, then keyed, no NLA: a solve under a live clip keys its pose rig.animation_data.action = None; poses = solve(rig, keys); rig.animation_data.action = bpy.data.actions.new(name); key_pose(rig, poses) bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath="/workspace/knight.glb", export_apply=True, export_animation_mode="ACTIONS") audit("/workspace/knight.glb", C)

poly count and bake time scale with it Pointiness, Bevel and AO wear are Cycles-only: bake them or make the damage geometric lighten (over its anchor, a heavy upload row, a slow world): plan in counts: each model's ctx.world.assets[ref].triangles × the rows placing it (.scene rows and the templates they point at; render: false draws nothing), ranked, summed against the anchor, spawn perf --frame for the frame's drawn total; lighten the file once and every placement follows: spawn fetch <ref>, Decimate (Collapse, ratio = target ÷ count), the export row's weld and smooth, one proof camera before and after (silhouette loss shows in pixels; none is the bar), export, spawn upload, point every row at the printed address, say the before and after count append a node group headless: with bpy.data.libraries.load(path, link=False) as (src, dst): dst.node_groups = [n for n in src.node_groups if "Scatter" in n] // obj.modifiers.new("x", "NODES").node_group = group; modifier inputs go by identifier, not name: {s.name: s.identifier for s in group.interface.items_tree if getattr(s, "in_out", "") == "INPUT"} add-ons: a tool Blender's natives lack is one install away: /opt/workshop/blender/provision-game-asset-addons.sh <id> (any extensions.blender.org id; →workshop) prints the module to enable per run under --factory-startup: bpy.ops.preferences.addon_enable(module="bl_ext.blender_org.<id>"); addon ops are plain bpy.ops on the selected, active object mpfb, a realistic human body on the rig the engine reads (no dial, remesh, big head or flat paint makes its face toon: a toon or restyle takes its art style's road, →geometry; any mixamo-named rig plays every library clip): from bl_ext.blender_org.mpfb.services import HumanService, TargetService; m = TargetService.get_default_macro_info_dict(); m.update({"age": 0.8, "weight": 0.9, "height": 0.2}); body = HumanService.create_human(macro_detail_dict=m); HumanService.add_builtin_rig(body, "mixamo") // dials 0..1: gender age muscle weight proportions height; default body 27k tris; "mixamo" only (→animations); its provision brings skins on this body's map, eyes, brows, lashes, hair, clothes: HumanService.set_character_skin and .add_mhclo_asset dress it as the provision prints voronoi fracture: bpy.ops.object.add_fracture_cell_objects(source_limit=40, margin=0.001) // pieces land beside the original; give the source a second slot first and aim the interior-material option at it; export whole + broken as two assets qm.qm_list() / qm.qm_apply(obj, tool, selection_attr=None, **params) // applies a NODES modifier: real geometry; cracks, holes, chunks eat closed solids, so select whole islands (qm_apply refuses an open patch) bake: bpy.ops.object.bake on Cycles // needs a UV map and each material's active Image Texture node on the target image, or bakes silently black; selected-to-active is a Cycles session per object: apply modifiers, keep Object coords in an attribute the materials read, join export: end GN graphs with Realize Instances (raw instances are exporter-fickle); weld and smooth-shade first: a flat-shaded export splits every edge into seams the engine's far levels cannot collapse; origin at each part's visual bottom center, placed there in the kit: the engine stands it on feetPosition; burial is y: { terrain: -X }, never a shifted origin. Blender's front (−Y) exports as glTF +Z: a thing built with a face is placed `model: { id, forward: "+z" }`; a rigged file's own facing is the `facing:` line `spawn upload` prints (→uploaded-models). A placed thing is solid only with `physics: "static"` (a walker: "character"), its collider cooked from the mesh junctions: a gable end-wall is a pentagon (-w/2,0) (w/2,0) (w/2,eave) (0,ridge) (-w/2,eave); sink roof slabs ~2 cm into the pitch plane, embed trim, sills and chimneys ≥ 3 cm into their host: overlap makes gaps impossible, exact contact misses blind; per-face color jitter reads as checkerboard, not age order (a roster): contract → donor measured → ONE hero at the proof (3/4, side, the extreme stride) approved → the others share the pipeline, never one body scaled and recoloured contract.json first (the shape above) // every script of the family reads it; scale ONCE from it: a source scale × a manifest scale doubles the body parts: garments, plates, weapons, shields are their own objects fitted to anatomy.json // plates overlap in the real order, seated ≥ 2 cm into their host; a rigid plate follows ONE bone, cloth deforms by weights with stride room in it; a weapon parents to its hand bone; live, children: [{ attachment: { bone: "RightHand" }, model }] seated in its `fist` (→uploaded-models) rig: one deform armature, Mixamo-style names (the ones the engine's IK, grounding and attachment resolve), positive scale, no root motion; weights proven at the extreme pose (knee, elbow, arm raised) in the proof BEFORE texture // a mirrored bone or a scaled armature exports a body that folds clips: Idle Walk Run Attack Hit Death // the placed row plays each by name (ctx.self.anim, →uploaded-models); a body you rigged carries its own clips audit: re-import the .glb into an empty scene (bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)), measure the deformed body in world space; the JSON chunk gives skins/joints, animations by name, one node per part, triangles vs the budget // the row you report IS these numbers

<samples> qm tools: cracks (engraved voronoi web), holes (noise gouges), chunks (voronoi removal), edge_wear, cables (sag between face regions), panel_cut, hull_cut, edges_to_ropes (rope along an edge path), selection_to_box, selection_to_cylinder add-ons by id: modular_tree, cell_fracture (a shatter), Bagapie (scatter, ivy) </samples>

import bpy, qm
scene = bpy.context.scene
scene.render.engine, scene.cycles.samples = "CYCLES", 8   # render.opengl refuses under -b; EEVEE renders in software
scene.render.resolution_x = scene.render.resolution_y = 656
wall = bpy.data.objects["Wall"]                       # JOINED blocks = islands; damage a duplicate, keep the pristine original
dmg = wall.data.attributes.new("dmg", "BOOLEAN", "POINT")
dmg.data.foreach_set("value", [v.co.x > 0 for v in wall.data.vertices])
qm.qm_apply(wall, "chunks", selection_attr="dmg")     # bites only the selected blocks; new faces take the LAST material slot
qm.qm_apply(wall, "cracks", Scale=4.0)                # params by socket name
for name, cam in (("a", "Cam34"), ("b", "CamGable"), ("c", "CamTop")):   # a turnaround: three 656-px views fill see's 2000 px, one alone renders at 1568
    scene.camera = bpy.data.objects[cam]
    scene.render.filepath = f"/tmp/proof/wall_{name}.png"
    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath="/workspace/wall.glb", export_apply=True)
dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get(); print("tris", sum(len(o.evaluated_get(dg).data.loop_triangles) for o in scene.objects if o.type == "MESH"))

import bpy, json                                       # art/knight/build.py: the character's one pass
C = json.load(open("art/knight/contract.json"))        # {"unit": "m", "height": 1.9, "feet": 0, "up": "+Z", "front": "-Y", "forward": "+z", "tris": 12000}
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath="/workspace/knight/body.glb")    # the body: mpfb (→api), your own, or a CDN base (→geometry)
body = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH" and o.vertex_groups)   # the skinned body, never the importer's bone widgets
dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get(); zs = sorted((body.matrix_world @ v.co).z for v in body.evaluated_get(dg).data.vertices)   # the deformed body in world space renders; body.scale moves a node no viewer draws
s = C["height"] / (zs[-1] - zs[0]); (body.find_armature() or body).scale = (s, s, s); bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="SELECT"); bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(scale=True)   # metres at scale 1; A = landmarks (hip, chest, shoulder) → anatomy.json
rig = mixamo_armature(A)
for o in (body, cuirass(A), pauldron(A, "L"), pauldron(A, "R"), gambeson(A)): o.modifiers.new("skin", "ARMATURE").object = rig
sword = longsword(); sword.parent, sword.parent_type, sword.parent_bone = rig, "BONE", "RightHand"   # the shield on LeftForeArm
for name, keys in CLIPS.items():                       # each clip, idle too, solved with none live, then keyed, no NLA: a solve under a live clip keys its pose
    rig.animation_data.action = None; poses = solve(rig, keys); rig.animation_data.action = bpy.data.actions.new(name); key_pose(rig, poses)
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath="/workspace/knight.glb", export_apply=True, export_animation_mode="ACTIONS")
audit("/workspace/knight.glb", C)
